Timeline/1969
1969Conference paper

Long-term memory

Remembering a story through relations

A system stored the relations in an English story so that it could answer questions about the story later.

Alan L. Tharp and Gilbert K. Krulee

The contribution

Tharp and Krulee converted sentences into predicates and property lists, organized relations across the passage, and used the resulting representation to answer inquiries. Their design explicitly addressed storage, retrieval, temporal organization, and priorities among remembered information. It is an early concrete treatment of memory as part of an interactive reasoning system.

What this does not establish

The work illustrates a constrained language and retrieval system, not unrestricted autobiographical memory. Its use of long-term memory describes the model rather than a demonstrated equivalence to human memory.

Why this date?

The original paper appears in the 1969 IJCAI proceedings. SHRDLU lists it as reference 54, with pages 579-586.

Cited by later work in the Atlas

  • SHRDLU grounds language in a small world (1971). Reference 54, printed page 462. Check the reference list.

These are verified references to the work or the publication version noted above. A citation alone does not establish that the later system implements the same method.
